data.content_ref: inline:The target asserts that surviving attempts to falsify a theory is what 'make[s] it the most informative error-eliminated option available.' This conflates a theory's corroboration (surviving tests) with its informative content. In critical rationalism, informative content (empirical content or falsifiability) is an a priori logical property determined by the set of basic statements the theory forbids, not a property acquired or maximized by surviving tests. A severely tested survivor is not more informative than a newly proposed, highly falsifiable conjecture; it is simply more corroborated. Because the target bases its preference for the survivor on a property (informativeness) that survival does not confer, its defense of the critical rationalist wager provides an incoherent Popperian justification.
